sentences.en: The earliest man?

sentences.en: Remarkable discovery in Sussex.
sentences.zh: 苏塞克斯郡的惊人发现。

sentences.en: A skull millions of years old.
sentences.zh: 一颗数百万年前的头骨。

sentences.zh: 苏塞克斯郡发现了我们这个时代最重要的史前发现之一。

sentences.en: In spite of the extreme secrecy of the authorities who are in possession of the relic, the news is leaking out

sentences.en: The facts are that a few weeks ago, men quarrying in a deep gravel pit turned up a human skull.
sentences.zh: 事实是，几周前，工人在一个深砾石坑采石时挖出了一颗人类头骨。

sentences.en: It was in fragments, but there was enough of it for the experts to form a conclusive judgment.
sentences.zh: 它已经碎了，但碎片足以让专家们做出结论性的判断。

sentences.en: It turns out to be the skull of a
sentences.zh: 结果证明这是一颗

sentences.en: Paleolithic man and is by far the earliest trace of mankind that has yet been found in England.
sentences.zh: 旧石器时代人类的头骨，是迄今为止在英国发现的最早的人类痕迹。

sentences.en: It was found in association with the bones of one of the most ancient types of elephant.
sentences.zh: 它与一种最古老的大象的骨骼一起被发现。

sentences.en: The stratum in which it lay was the beach of a very old riverbed.
sentences.zh: 它所在的岩层是一条非常古老的河床的河滩。

sentences.en: There is no doubt at all of its authenticity.
sentences.zh: 它的真实性毫无疑问。

sentences.en: The skull resembles the Neanderthal specimen, but belongs to a much lower and more primitive type of mankind even than that.
sentences.zh: 这颗头骨类似于尼安德特人的标本，但属于比那更低等、更原始的人类类型。

sentences.en: It was certainly a very different brain to that possessed by any living race.
sentences.zh: 它肯定与任何现存种族所拥有的大脑截然不同。

sentences.zh: 专家们不敢对苏塞克斯人的年代发表意见，但很可能他生活在数百万年前。

sentences.zh: 这是一种英美融合。

sentences.en: It's an attempt to build a sense of Atlantic identity that nevertheless makes the British feel slightly like they're being put in the shade by American advances.
sentences.zh: 这是一种建立大西洋身份感的尝试，但尽管如此，还是让英国人觉得他们稍微被美国的进步所掩盖了。

sentences.en: And then of course, you have human fossils.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有人类化石。

sentences.en: And this is very much a live area, not least because of Darwin's book about it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常活跃的领域，尤其是因为达尔文关于它的书。

sentences.en: But the idea that humans have evolved, you need fossil evidence for it.
sentences.zh: 但人类已经进化的想法，你需要化石证据。

sentences.en: And this has begun to appear over the course of the second half of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 这在19世纪下半叶开始出现。

sentences.en: So in 1856, a skull has been found in the Neander Valley, the Neanderthal.
sentences.zh: 所以1856年，在尼安德特山谷发现了一个头骨，即尼安德特人。

sentences.en: So that's where the name of Neanderthal Man comes from, and that's German.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是尼安德特人名字的由来，那是德国的。

sentences.en: 1868, a prehistoric Homo Sapien has been found at Cro-Magnon in France.
sentences.zh: 1868年，在法国的克罗马农发现了一个史前智人。

sentences.en: Is that a place?
sentences.zh: 那是一个地方吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Cro-Magnon is a place.
sentences.zh: 克罗马农是一个地方。

sentences.en: Who knew?
sentences.zh: 谁能想到呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, I've learned something.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我学到了一些东西。

sentences.en: I'm absolutely thrilled with that.
sentences.zh: 对此我感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And then in 1886, some Neanderthal skulls are found in Belgium.
sentences.zh: 然后在1886年，在比利时发现了一些尼安德特人的头骨。

sentences.en: So Germany, France, Belgium.
sentences.zh: 所以是德国、法国、比利时。

sentences.en: Who would have imagined that they would be full of Neanderthals, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，谁能想到它们会到处都是尼安德特人呢？

sentences.en: But Dominic, nothing in Britain.
sentences.zh: 但是多米尼克，英国什么都没有。

sentences.en: That does not surprise me.
sentences.zh: 这倒不让我感到惊讶。

sentences.en: So Britain lacks a prehistoric man.
sentences.zh: 所以英国缺乏史前人类。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: No Neanderthals in Britain.
sentences.zh: 英国没有尼安德特人。

sentences.en: And this is a massive, massive sore point for British scientists.
sentences.zh: 这对英国科学家来说是一个非常、非常痛心的问题。

sentences.en: And there's a kind of an additional complication, an additional reason why British scientists are getting a
sentences.zh: 还有一个额外的复杂情况，一个让英国科学家感到

sentences.en: bit antsy, is that in 1891, there'd been a very, very controversial find made outside
sentences.zh: 有些焦躁的额外原因，那就是在1891年，在欧洲之外

sentences.en: Europe in Java, so in Indonesia, by a Dutch expedition.
sentences.zh: 的爪哇，也就是印度尼西亚，由一支荷兰探险队做出了一个非常、非常有争议的发现。

sentences.en: And they'd found the remains of what the discovery is called Java Man, which seems to be a kind of human ape missing link.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了被称为“爪哇人”的遗骸，这似乎是一种人类与猿类之间的缺失环节。

sentences.en: And Java Man is bipedal.
sentences.zh: 而且爪哇人是双足行走的。

sentences.en: So it seems to walk on, you know, two feet, but it has a very small skull.
sentences.zh: 所以它似乎是用，你知道，双脚走路，但它的头骨非常小。

sentences.en: And European scientists are very sceptical about this.
sentences.zh: 欧洲科学家对此非常怀疑。

sentences.en: And they insist it's not human at all, that it's just an ape.
sentences.zh: 他们坚持认为它根本不是人类，只是猿类。

sentences.en: Because their assumption is that big brains come first and then walking on two feet.
sentences.zh: 因为他们的假设是，大脑发达在先，双足行走在后。

sentences.en: And the reason that they argue this is chiefly because it then enables them to argue, based on the fossil evidence of the Neanderthals and the Cro-Magnons,
sentences.zh: 他们之所以这样争论，主要是因为这使他们能够基于尼安德特人和克罗马农人的化石证据，

sentences.en: that humans originated in Europe.
sentences.zh: 论证人类起源于欧洲。

sentences.en: Because at this point, there is no evidence at all that humans have originated in Africa, even though actually Darwin thinks that they did because
sentences.zh: 因为在这一点上，根本没有证据表明人类起源于非洲，尽管达尔文实际上认为他们起源于非洲，因为

sentences.en: that's where all the apes are found.
sentences.zh: 那是所有猿类被发现的地方。

sentences.en: And this, again, is important for European kind of self-esteem because it enables them to explain why Europeans are the most advanced of races as they see it.
sentences.zh: 而这一点，对于欧洲人的自尊心来说再次显得很重要，因为它使他们能够解释为什么在他们看来欧洲人是最高级的种族。

sentences.en: Because they were born first and they're further along.
sentences.zh: 因为他们出生得早，而且进化得更远。

sentences.en: That's basically the claim, is it?
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是他们的主张，对吧？

sentences.en: That's basically the claim.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是他们的主张。

sentences.en: I'm slightly baffled about the bipedalism and why that matters.
sentences.zh: 我对双足行走以及为什么这很重要感到有些困惑。

sentences.en: Because the Neanderthals and the Cro-Magnons are bipedal and they have relatively large heads.
sentences.zh: 因为尼安德特人和克罗马农人是双足行走的，而且他们有相对较大的头颅。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Java man, if it's bipedal and has a small head, that suggests that humans would have originated outside Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以爪哇人，如果它是双足行走且头颅较小，那这就暗示人类起源于欧洲之外。

sentences.en: And that can't be true.
sentences.zh: 而那不可能是真的。

sentences.en: Well, they don't want to believe that because they want to believe that humans emerged in Europe.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们不想相信这一点，因为他们想相信人类是在欧洲出现的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because it then enables them to argue that Europeans are the most superior race.
sentences.zh: 因为这使他们能够争辩说欧洲人是最优越的种族。

sentences.en: So they're saying, OK, sure, there's a fellow walking around on two feet, but he's got a tiny brain, so he doesn't count.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说，好吧，当然，有个家伙在用双脚走来走去，但他大脑很小，所以他不算数。

sentences.en: It's a monkey.
sentences.zh: 那是只猴子。

sentences.en: It's an ape.
sentences.zh: 那是只猿。

sentences.en: It's nothing to do with humans.
sentences.zh: 它和人类毫无关系。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's their argument.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的论点。

sentences.en: And it's an argument that is clearly driven basically by racism and by a sense of European superiority.
sentences.zh: 而且这个论点显然基本上是由种族主义和一种欧洲优越感所驱动的。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And that in turn explains why British scientists are desperate to find human fossil remains in Britain and particularly human fossil remains that have big skulls,
sentences.zh: 这反过来解释了为什么英国科学家急于在英国寻找人类化石遗骸，特别是那些拥有大头骨的人类化石遗骸，

sentences.en: because both national and racial pride is essentially riding on it.
sentences.zh: 因为民族自豪感和种族自豪感本质上都寄托在它上面。

sentences.en: The bigger the head, the better.
sentences.zh: 头越大越好。

sentences.en: The bigger the head, the more British, the better it is.
sentences.zh: 头越大，越英国，就越好。

sentences.en: I've got a massive head, Tom, if that's any inspiration to you.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，如果这对你有什么启发的话，我的头可是很大的。

sentences.en: Well, there you go.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你看。

sentences.en: I have to have like a baseball cap or something in a special size because my head is so big.
sentences.zh: 我必须戴那种特殊尺寸的棒球帽之类的东西，因为我的头太大了。

sentences.en: Massive brain.
sentences.zh: 大脑巨大。

sentences.en: And you're bipedal.
sentences.zh: 而且你是双足行走的。

sentences.en: Well, sometimes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有时候是。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Anyway, yeah.
sentences.zh: 总之，是啊。

sentences.en: So basically, this is the kind of the context for the sensational discovery announced in The Guardian.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这就是《卫报》宣布的那项轰动性发现的背景。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's why The Guardian is so keen on emphasising that the skull is big.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么《卫报》如此热衷于强调那个头骨很大。

sentences.en: So The Guardian doesn't say who has found it.
sentences.zh: 所以《卫报》没有说是谁发现了它。

sentences.en: It just says there has been a find near Piltdown in Sussex.
sentences.zh: 它只是说在苏塞克斯郡的皮尔特当附近有一个发现。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I think I'm right in saying that a month later, the two blokes who have found it pitch up at the Geological Society in London and say, here we are.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我说得没错，一个月后，那两个发现它的人出现在伦敦的地质学会，说，我们来了。

sentences.en: And this is the amazing finding.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个惊人的发现。

sentences.en: And who are they?
sentences.zh: 他们是谁？

sentences.en: Well, so as you say, two people kind of jointly make this presentation on the 18th of December 1912.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你所说，1912年12月18日，两个人共同做了这个展示。

sentences.en: And the first person there is the guy who had made the initial find.
sentences.zh: 第一个人就是最初做出发现的那个家伙。

sentences.en: He discovered a fragment of skull at Piltdown.
sentences.zh: 他在皮尔特当发现了一块头骨碎片。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Charles Dawson.
sentences.zh: 这个家伙叫查尔斯·道森。

sentences.en: And he is actually not a scientist at all, but a country solicitor.
sentences.zh: 他实际上根本不是科学家，而是一名乡村律师。

sentences.en: And he has his practice in Uckfield, not far from Lewis.
sentences.zh: 他在离刘易斯不远的阿克菲尔德执业。

sentences.en: And to this day, I gather, Dawson Hart and company solicitors can still be found.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，直到今天，道森·哈特律师事务所仍然存在。

sentences.en: So that's very exciting.
sentences.zh: 那真是太令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, let's hope that this story inspires confidence in them, Tom.
sentences.zh: 好吧，汤姆，希望这个故事能让他们建立信心。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Let's hope.
sentences.zh: 让我们希望如此。

sentences.en: So Charles Dawson, basically, he has the look of a boiled egg with a moustache.
sentences.zh: 所以查尔斯·道森，基本上，他看起来就像一个长了胡子的水煮蛋。

sentences.en: Like O'Keele Poirot.
sentences.zh: 就像波洛侦探。

sentences.en: Very like O'Keele Poirot.
sentences.zh: 非常像波洛侦探。

sentences.en: In appearance, he's kind of very jovial.
sentences.zh: 在外表上，他显得非常快活。

sentences.en: There's a faint twinkle in his eye, it is often said.
sentences.zh: 人们常说，他的眼睛里闪烁着微弱的光芒。

sentences.en: Love it.
sentences.zh: 喜欢这个。

sentences.en: The scientists who work with him on Piltdown Man all think he's great.
sentences.zh: 在皮尔特当人项目上与他共事的科学家都认为他很棒。

sentences.en: So one of them describes him as a delightful colleague.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人形容他是一位令人愉快的同事。

sentences.en: Another says of him, he's always cheerful, hopeful, and overflowing with enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 另一个人评价他：他总是开朗、充满希望，热情洋溢。

sentences.en: And his wife, they have a very happy marriage.
sentences.zh: 还有他的妻子，他们的婚姻非常幸福。

sentences.en: She says of him that he's the best and kindest man who ever lived.
sentences.zh: 她评价他是这辈子最好、最善良的人。

sentences.en: So if the listeners want to kind of aid memoir, he's very like me.
sentences.zh: 所以如果听众想找个记忆辅助，他非常像我。

sentences.en: Are you a boiled egg with a moustache?
sentences.zh: 你是一个长了胡子的水煮蛋吗？

sentences.en: I don't have a moustache.
sentences.zh: 我没有胡子。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: So as well as looking like a boiled egg with a moustache, he's also distinguished for his insatiable curiosity about every aspect of the natural history and history and archaeology
sentences.zh: 所以除了长得像个长了胡子的水煮蛋，他还以对苏塞克斯郡自然历史、历史和考古学的各个方面有着贪得无厌的好奇心而著称，

sentences.en: of Sussex, which is a country very rich in all three of those things.
sentences.zh: 苏塞克斯郡在这三方面都非常丰富。

sentences.en: So he is a leading light of, Dominic, the country's oldest county archaeological society, which is the Sussex Archaeological Society.
sentences.zh: 所以他是多米尼克，该郡最古老的县考古学会——苏塞克斯考古学会的领军人物。

sentences.en: It's still going strong, a tremendous organization.
sentences.zh: 它至今依然活跃，是一个了不起的组织。

sentences.en: And like Gideon Mantel, the discoverer of the Iguanodon, he lives in Lewis and specifically in a very grand house at the foot of Lewis Castle called Castle Lodge.
sentences.zh: 而且像禽龙的发现者吉迪恩·曼特尔一样，他住在刘易斯，具体来说是住在刘易斯城堡脚下一座非常宏伟的房子里，叫城堡小屋。

sentences.en: So he's very much at the heart of Sussex's history.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常处于苏塞克斯历史的核心。

sentences.en: And over the course of his career, he has made a succession of absolutely amazing discoveries.
sentences.zh: 在他的职业生涯中，他做出了一连串绝对惊人的发现。

sentences.en: So he's found fossils like Mantel had done.
sentences.zh: 所以他像曼特尔一样发现了化石。

sentences.en: And specifically, he had discovered the tooth of a previously unknown species of mammal from
sentences.zh: 具体来说，他发现了一种此前未知的哺乳动物的牙齿，来自

sentences.en: the Cretaceous period, which is the last of the three periods of the age of the dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 白垩纪，这是恐龙时代三个时期中的最后一个。

sentences.en: He's discovered lots of antiquities.
sentences.zh: 他发现了很多古物。

sentences.en: And all of these have kind of shed intriguing and unexpected light on obscure periods of history.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都以一种引人入胜且出人意料的方式照亮了历史上晦暗不明的时期。

sentences.en: So he's found a Roman statuette that is made of cast iron rather than wrought iron, which is what you would expect.
sentences.zh: 所以他发现了一尊罗马小雕像，它是铸铁做的，而不是你所预期的锻铁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Because it is assumed that cast iron techniques had only developed in England in the 14th century.
sentences.zh: 因为人们认为铸铁技术直到14世纪才在英国发展起来。

sentences.en: So to discover that the Romans had been on top of it is, you know, it's an amazing find.
sentences.zh: 所以发现罗马人早就掌握了这一点，你知道，这是一个惊人的发现。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Brilliant to have overturned conventional wisdom of academics, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 推翻学术界的传统智慧真是太棒了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And Dawson has also found a brick from Pevensey, which is stamped with what seems to be the very last dateable Roman inscription ever found in Britain.
sentences.zh: 道森还从佩文西发现了一块砖，上面盖着似乎是英国发现的最后一个可考证日期的罗马铭文。

sentences.en: So that, again, is amazing.
sentences.zh: 所以那，再次强调，真是太惊人了。

sentences.en: He's found a stone axe.
sentences.zh: 他发现了一把石斧。

sentences.en: He's found the remains of an ancient boat.
sentences.zh: 他发现了古代船只的残骸。

sentences.en: So all incredible.
sentences.zh: 所以一切都令人难以置信。

sentences.en: Lots more along those lines.
sentences.zh: 还有很多类似的东西。

sentences.en: And he's also very keen on natural wonders, of which the most extraordinary is a toad that has been mummified inside stone.
sentences.zh: 而且他还非常热衷于自然奇观，其中最非凡的是一只在石头里木乃伊化的蟾蜍。

sentences.en: So extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 真是太非凡了。

sentences.en: Amazing wonder.
sentences.zh: 惊人的奇迹。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: How can that even happen?
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能发生呢？

sentences.en: I'm curious about that, but we'll put it on one side, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我对那个很好奇，但我想我们还是先把它放在一边吧。

sentences.en: But not the rest is toads.
sentences.zh: 但剩下的可不是蟾蜍。

sentences.en: It's just a kind of slew of amazing things that he's discovered that has won him lots of honours.
sentences.zh: 这只是一连串他发现的惊人事物，为他赢得了许多荣誉。

sentences.en: So he's been elected to the Society of Antiquaries in London, like me.
sentences.zh: 所以他像我一样被选入了伦敦古物协会。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You're kind of very similar, kind of forensic attention to detail and authenticity, right?
sentences.zh: 你们非常相似，对细节和真实性有着法医般的关注，对吧？

sentences.en: We will see.
sentences.zh: 我们走着瞧。

sentences.en: And in Sussex, he's hailed by the local press as the wizard of Sussex for his almost supernatural ability to pluck these incredible finds as if from nowhere.
sentences.zh: 在苏塞克斯，他被当地媒体誉为“苏塞克斯巫师”，因为他有一种近乎超自然的能力，能凭空变出这些令人难以置信的发现。

sentences.en: So amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: And his renown is such that basically, I don't know when he has time to do his soliciting.
sentences.zh: 他的名声如此之大，以至于基本上，我不知道他哪有时间去处理他的法律事务。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, he doesn't seem to be very keen on the law at all because he's hanging out with all kinds of luminaries.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他似乎一点也不热衷于法律，因为他整天和各种名流混在一起。

sentences.en: So one of these, perhaps the most distinguished of these luminaries, is a man called Arthur
sentences.zh: 所以其中一位，也许是这些名流中最杰出的一位，是一个叫亚瑟·

sentences.en: Smith Woodward.
sentences.zh: 史密斯·伍德沃德的人。

sentences.en: And he is the keeper of geology at the Natural History Museum.
sentences.zh: 他是自然历史博物馆的地质学馆长。

sentences.en: And he, Dominic, is a world expert on fossil fish.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，他是一位世界级的化石鱼类专家。

sentences.en: God, he sounds such an interesting man, Tom.
sentences.zh: 天哪，汤姆，他听起来真是个有趣的人。

sentences.en: Well, he is because he's not just an expert on fossil fish.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他确实是，因为他不仅是化石鱼类专家。

sentences.en: He is also sufficiently brilliant that he is the guy who Dawson gives the Cretaceous mammal tooth to, which he'd found back in 1891.
sentences.zh: 他足够聪明，以至于道森把他在1891年发现的那颗白垩纪哺乳动物牙齿交给了他。

sentences.en: And Woodward had been very excited about it and realised that it was a hitherto unknown species.
sentences.zh: 伍德沃德对此非常兴奋，并意识到这是一个迄今为止未知的物种。

sentences.en: And so since then, they've become great friends.
sentences.zh: 所以从那时起，他们就成了好朋友。

sentences.en: Dawson is always getting in touch with Woodward to tell him about his latest finds.
sentences.zh: 道森总是联系伍德沃德，告诉他他最新的发现。

sentences.en: And what's impressive about this friendship is that Woodward is not a very clubbable man.
sentences.zh: 这段友谊令人印象深刻的是，伍德沃德并不是一个很善于交际的人。

sentences.en: He's very tall.
sentences.zh: 他个子很高。

sentences.en: He's gaunt.
sentences.zh: 他面容憔悴。

sentences.en: He's fussy.
sentences.zh: 他很挑剔。

sentences.en: He's acerbic.
sentences.zh: 他说话尖刻。

sentences.en: Tom, this is unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这简直令人难以置信。

sentences.en: This is the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是播客。

sentences.en: That's what it is.
sentences.zh: 事实就是这样。

sentences.en: He has a thin goat-like beard.
sentences.zh: 他留着一撮山羊胡子。

sentences.en: It's uncanny.
sentences.zh: 真是不可思议。

sentences.en: Which I absolutely don't.
sentences.zh: 而我绝对没有。

sentences.en: And actually, Dominic, he's not like me.
sentences.zh: 事实上，多米尼克，他和我并不像。

sentences.en: He's like Professor Summerlee in The Lost World by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle.
sentences.zh: 他就像阿瑟·柯南·道尔爵士所著《失落的世界》里的萨默利教授。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which I'm sure lots of people have read, but if you haven't, it was published in 1912.
sentences.zh: 我相信很多人都读过，但如果你没读过，这本书出版于1912年。

sentences.en: So the same year that Piltdown Man was found.
sentences.zh: 也就是皮尔特道恩人被发现的那一年。

sentences.en: And it describes an expedition of two scientists.
sentences.zh: 书中描述了一次由两位科学家进行的探险。

sentences.en: One of whom is Professor Summerlee, a journalist and a big game hunter, to go and discover a lost world in South America on a plateau.
sentences.zh: 其中一位是萨默利教授，还有一位记者和一位大型猎物猎人，他们去南美洲的一个高原上寻找一个失落的世界。

sentences.en: What an amazing coincidence that The Lost World was published, presumably just months before this discovery.
sentences.zh: 《失落的世界》在这一发现前几个月出版，这真是个惊人的巧合。

sentences.en: Yes, it is a coincidence.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实是个巧合。

sentences.en: Not least because as well as dinosaurs, The Lost World features ape men who were cast as missing links.
sentences.zh: 尤其是因为《失落的世界》不仅有恐龙，还有被视为“缺失环节”的猿人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what is even more of a coincidence is that the author, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, who, of course, is also the author of Sherlock Holmes, lives some eight miles from Piltdown.
sentences.zh: 更巧的是，作者阿瑟·柯南·道尔爵士——当然也是福尔摩斯的作者——就住在离皮尔特道恩大约八英里远的地方。

sentences.en: So Conan Doyle's a great walker.
sentences.zh: 所以柯南·道尔是个很爱走路的人。

sentences.en: That's very much within walkable distance for him.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，这完全在步行距离之内。

sentences.en: And Conan Doyle has met both Dawson and Woodward because Conan Doyle, I mean, he's interested in everything, basically very interested in palatology.
sentences.zh: 而且柯南·道尔见过道森和伍德沃德，因为柯南·道尔，我的意思是，他什么都感兴趣，基本上对古生物学非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: He'd found some dinosaur footprints and he'd got Dawson over to have a look at them.
sentences.zh: 他发现了一些恐龙足迹，还叫道森过去看了看。

sentences.en: And they've become sufficiently good friends that in November 1911, Conan Doyle invites
sentences.zh: 他们成了很好的朋友，以至于在1911年11月，柯南·道尔邀请了

sentences.en: Dawson and his wife for lunch.
sentences.zh: 道森和他的妻子共进午餐。

sentences.en: So they go over.
sentences.zh: 于是他们去了。

sentences.en: And almost certainly at this lunch, they discuss missing links.
sentences.zh: 几乎可以肯定，在这次午餐中，他们讨论了“缺失环节”。

sentences.en: Conan Doyle seems to have told Dawson about his plans for The Lost World.
sentences.zh: 柯南·道尔似乎已经告诉了道森他关于《失落的世界》的计划。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And after the discovery is made, after the finding of Piltdown Man, Dawson writes to Woodward, huge excitement.
sentences.zh: 在发现之后，在找到皮尔特道恩人之后，道森写信给伍德沃德，非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Conan Doyle has written and seems excited about the skull.
sentences.zh: 柯南·道尔写了信，似乎对这个头骨很兴奋。

sentences.en: He has kindly offered to drive me in his motor anywhere.
sentences.zh: 他好心地提出要开车带我去任何地方。

sentences.en: So Conan Doyle is also part of the Piltdown Man set.
sentences.zh: 所以柯南·道尔也是皮尔特道恩人圈子的一员。

sentences.en: Yeah, the Piltdown Set.
sentences.zh: 是的，皮尔特道恩圈子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: So how had Dawson actually come to find the skull itself?
sentences.zh: 那么道森究竟是怎么发现这个头骨本身的呢？

sentences.en: So at this meeting on the 18th of December 1912 at the Geological Society, he gives his first account of what had happened.
sentences.zh: 在1912年12月18日地质学会的会议上，他第一次讲述了事情的经过。

sentences.en: And he reports that workmen had been working in a gravel pit in Piltdown.
sentences.zh: 他报告说，工人们一直在皮尔特道恩的一个砾石坑里工作。

sentences.en: And because they knew of his reputation as someone interested in such things, they had given him a small piece of bone that the workmen had found in the pit.
sentences.zh: 因为他们知道他以对这类事情感兴趣而闻名，所以他们给了他一小块工人在坑里发现的骨头。

sentences.en: And at this meeting, Dawson is very vague as to when exactly this had happened.
sentences.zh: 在这次会议上，道森对于这具体是什么时候发生的说得很模糊。

sentences.en: So, I mean, it could have been any time, you know, from kind of 1899 onwards.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可能是任何时候，你知道，从1899年左右开始。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the next morning it's reported that he had said that he had been given this in 1908.
sentences.zh: 但第二天有报道称，他说这是他在1908年得到的。

sentences.en: I've been hanging on to this bit of skull for four years.
sentences.zh: 我把这块头骨碎片留了四年。

sentences.en: I suppose you might.
sentences.zh: 我想你可能会这样做。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the reason for this, he says, is that it was only a fragment and that the workmen had said that they had originally found a much larger skull, which they had then smashed
sentences.zh: 他说之所以这样，是因为这只是一个碎片，工人们说他们最初发现了一个大得多的头骨，然后他们把它砸碎了，

sentences.en: because they thought that it was a coconut.
sentences.zh: 因为他们以为那是一个椰子。

sentences.en: A coconut in Sussex.
sentences.zh: 萨塞克斯郡的一个椰子。

sentences.en: A fossil coconut in Sussex.
sentences.zh: 萨塞克斯郡的一个化石椰子。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And so therefore, knowing this, Dawson, he's going to the quarry looking for the other fragments of this skull that has been smashed by the workmen.
sentences.zh: 所以，知道了这一点，道森去采石场寻找被工人们砸碎的头骨的其他碎片。

sentences.en: And over the course of the four years, if it is four years, he's gradually found them and he's pieced them together.
sentences.zh: 在四年时间里，如果真的是四年，他逐渐找到了它们，并把它们拼凑在一起。

sentences.en: And it makes a kind of an entire cranium of an unusual thickness.
sentences.zh: 它构成了一个完整的、厚度异常的颅骨。

sentences.en: So much thicker than a normal skull would be.
sentences.zh: 比普通头骨厚得多。

sentences.en: And by 1912, you know, he's ready basically to announce it to the world.
sentences.zh: 到了1912年，你知道，他基本上准备好向世界宣布了。

sentences.en: And so he writes a letter to Woodward telling him about Conan Doyle and about the lost world and how it's coming out.
sentences.zh: 于是他写信给伍德沃德，告诉他关于柯南·道尔和《失落的世界》以及它即将出版的消息。

sentences.en: And then he just, this kind of casual mention, he says, I found a portion of a human skull and he compares it to a Neanderthal skull, which of course, to any British scientist is
sentences.zh: 然后他只是随口提了一句，他说，我发现了一部分人类头骨，并把它与尼安德特人的头骨进行了比较，这对任何英国科学家来说，当然是

sentences.en: an absolute way of saying, I might've found a British Neanderthal skull.
sentences.zh: 一种绝对的暗示，即我可能发现了一个英国的尼安德特人头骨。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So exciting.
sentences.zh: 太令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: So exciting.
sentences.zh: 太令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: You know, we can put the Germans in the shade here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们可以让德国人相形见绌了。

sentences.en: And Woodward is certainly intrigued by this, but he doesn't actually get down to Piltdown for quite a while.
sentences.zh: 伍德沃德当然对此很感兴趣，但他很长一段时间都没有去皮尔特道恩。

sentences.en: And this is partly because, as I said, the weather is so bad.
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为，正如我所说，天气太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And it's also because, you know, he's a busy man, he's in charge of an entire department in the Natural History Museum, doesn't have the time.
sentences.zh: 这也是因为，你知道，他是个大忙人，他负责自然历史博物馆的一个完整部门，没有时间。

sentences.en: And it's clear that Dawson is getting a bit impatient about this.
sentences.zh: 很明显，道森对此有点不耐烦了。

sentences.en: He wants to show off his discovery.
sentences.zh: 他想炫耀他的发现。

sentences.en: So on the 24th of May, he goes to Woodward and he shows him all the fragments of the skull.
sentences.zh: 所以5月24日，他去找伍德沃德，展示了头骨的所有碎片。

sentences.en: And Woodward is pretty excited now.
sentences.zh: 伍德沃德现在非常兴奋。

sentences.en: So on the 2nd of June, he joins Dawson at Piltdown to start on the excavations.
sentences.zh: 于是6月2日，他加入道森在皮尔特道恩开始挖掘工作。

sentences.en: And it's brilliantly Edwardian that the first day they don't get much done because they're having a huge picnic.
sentences.zh: 这非常具有爱德华时代的风格，第一天他们没做什么，因为他们举行了一场盛大的野餐。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Very wind in the willows.
sentences.zh: 非常有《柳林风声》的感觉。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Lattice pork pies and lemonade and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 格子猪肉馅饼、柠檬水之类的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they start their excavations and they don't find anything to begin with.
sentences.zh: 他们开始挖掘，起初什么也没发现。

sentences.en: They're kind of sifting through both the quarry itself, but all the piles of kind of refuse that the workmen have left because presumably this is where other bits might be.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在筛查采石场本身，以及工人们留下的所有垃圾堆，因为推测其他碎片可能就在那里。

sentences.en: And they're working and working, working.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在工作，一直在工作。

sentences.en: And then on the 23rd of June, so that's basically three weeks of working and they're not working all the time.
sentences.zh: 然后在6月23日，也就是基本上工作了三周，而且他们并不是一直在工作。

sentences.en: They're mainly working at the weekends.
sentences.zh: 他们主要是在周末工作。

sentences.en: Dawson finds this jaw, the jaw that looks like a chimpanzee jaw.
sentences.zh: 道森发现了这个下颚，那个看起来像黑猩猩下颚的下颚。

sentences.en: And it fits, it seems, with the skull.
sentences.zh: 而且它似乎与头骨吻合。

sentences.en: And over the course of July, they find shaped flints.
sentences.zh: 在七月期间，他们发现了成形的燧石。

sentences.en: So these are the tools that presumably have been used by the Piltdown man and bones of various prehistoric animals that kind of enable them to date it as being much further back
sentences.zh: 这些就是推测皮尔特道恩人使用的工具，还有各种史前动物的骨头，这使他们能够将其年代定为比尼安德特人更久远，

sentences.en: in time than Neanderthal man.
sentences.zh: 在时间上更早。

sentences.en: So clearly this man is much older than the German fossil man.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，这个人比德国的化石人要古老得多。

sentences.en: So, you know, this is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这太棒了。

sentences.en: And it is Woodward who's been working with Dawson throughout the summer, who joins Dawson at the meeting of the Geological Society.
sentences.zh: 正是整个夏天与道森一起工作的伍德沃德，加入了道森在地质学会的会议。

sentences.en: And this is crucial for the repute of what is being said because Dawson had actually become president of the Geological Society in 1904.
sentences.zh: 这对所说内容的声誉至关重要，因为道森实际上在1904年成为了地质学会的主席。

sentences.en: And it's his prestige, of course, that makes the news of the discovery echo around Britain, across the world.
sentences.zh: 当然，正是他的声望使得这一发现的消息在英国乃至全世界引起了轰动。

sentences.en: And brilliantly from Dawson's point of view, it is Woodward who pays tribute to the role that he's played in the discovery of this amazing find by giving Piltdown man the official
sentences.zh: 从道森的角度来看，非常精彩的是，正是伍德沃德通过给皮尔特道恩人赋予正式的科学名称，

sentences.en: scientific name of Eoanthropus dorsoni.
sentences.zh: 即“道森曙人”（Eoanthropus dawsoni），来表彰他在这一惊人发现中所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: So Dawson's dawn man.
sentences.zh: 也就是道森的曙人。

sentences.en: So, you know, he now has this incredible fossil named after him.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他现在以这个令人难以置信的化石命名。

sentences.en: So it's an amazing story about kind of amateur archaeologists and kind of antiquarian, you know, in the English countryside, who's teamed up with a really well-respected scientific
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个关于英国乡村的业余考古学家和古物研究者，与一位真正受人尊敬的科学头脑合作的惊人故事。

sentences.en: mind.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And together they have revolutionized the way people think about life on Earth.
sentences.zh: 他们共同彻底改变了人们对地球生命的看法。

sentences.en: They have.
sentences.zh: 他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: But also they've shown that the tradition that Gideon Mantel had embodied, you know, the doctor who goes out and finds a dinosaur, that that tradition is still absolutely living
sentences.zh: 但他们也表明，吉迪恩·曼特尔所体现的传统，你知道，那个出去发现恐龙的医生，这种传统在一百年后的萨塞克斯郡田野里依然绝对鲜活且有效。

sentences.en: and valid in the fields of Sussex a hundred years on.
sentences.zh: 这让英国人感到安心，你知道，他们仍然处于领先地位。

sentences.en: And it's a reassurance to the British, you know, that they're still the cutting edge.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然是顶尖的国家。

sentences.en: They're still top nation.
sentences.zh: 所以受到了巨大的热情欢迎。

sentences.en: So greeted with huge enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 因此，不出所料，你知道，挖掘工作在第二年恢复了，一直持续到

sentences.zh: 1913年，贯穿1914年的夏天，即使多米尼克，战争的乌云正在聚集。

sentences.en: 1913, through the summer of 1914, even Dominic as the storm clouds of war are gathering.
sentences.zh: 并且又有一些进一步的发现。

sentences.en: And various further finds are made.
sentences.zh: 比如鼻骨，据我所知非常重要，还有犬齿，你知道，一颗牙齿，这再次显然非常重要，原因我不完全理解。

sentences.en: So nasal bones, which I gather are very important, and a canine, you know, a tooth, which again is apparently very significant for reasons I don't entirely understand.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，伍德沃德的论点已经得到了广泛的接受，特别是下颚和头骨属于同一个体。

sentences.en: And by this point, there's pretty much widespread acceptance of Woodward's arguments, particularly that the jaw and the skull go together.
sentences.zh: 特别是在美国，有一些科学家认为它们可能是被混在一起的不同物种。

sentences.en: There are scientists in America, particularly, who argue that perhaps they're different species who've been jumbled up.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人，特别是在欧洲，都接受这一点，证明了大脑是在双足行走之前进化的。

sentences.en: But most people accept, particularly in Europe, that this proves that the big brain evolved before bipedalism.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 所以即使是德国人也接受了。

sentences.en: So even the Germans.
sentences.zh: 是的，即使是德国人。

sentences.en: Yeah, even the Germans.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是他们一直在寻找的东西。

sentences.en: It's what they basically, they've all been kind of looking for.
sentences.zh: 现在，当然，地平线上有几朵可能的乌云，可能表明并非一切都如其所见。

sentences.en: Now, there are, of course, a couple of possible clouds on the horizon, possible indications that not everything is quite what it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 其中第一个发生在1914年6月下旬。

sentences.en: And the first of these happens in late June 1914.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，第一次世界大战的前奏。

sentences.en: So, you know, the build up to the First World War.
sentences.zh: 伍德沃德在他那本标题精彩的书《最早的英国人》中描述了一个特定的时刻。

sentences.en: And a particular moment that Woodward describes in his brilliantly titled book, The Earliest
sentences.zh: 我正在观察那个使用宽镐或鹤嘴锄的工人，这时我看到一些被一击打碎的小骨头碎片散落开来。

sentences.en: Englishman.
sentences.zh: 我停止了他的工作，用手搜寻那个地方，拉出了一块沉重的骨刃，他损坏了它的末端。

sentences.en: I was watching the workman who was using a broad pick or mattock when I saw some small splinters of bones scattered by a blow.
sentences.zh: 这块沉重的骨刃有些非常奇怪的地方，伍德沃德本人在书中也指出了这一点，那就是它看起来完全像板球拍。

sentences.en: I stopped his work and searching the spot with my hands, pulled out a heavy blade of bone of which he had damaged the end.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，怪异地像。

sentences.zh: 用石头做的。

sentences.en: I mean, eerily.
sentences.zh: 用象骨做的。

sentences.en: Made of stone.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 那么皮尔特道恩人拿着板球拍在做什么？

sentences.zh: 只是个巧合，汤姆。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a question that the outbreak of war kind of slightly buries.
sentences.zh: 然后还有另一个巧合，发生在两年后的1916年8月，非常令人悲伤的是，道森去世了。

sentences.en: Just a coincidence, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他才52岁，死于恶性贫血。

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 从那时起，现场再也没有发现任何化石。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 他在一场一级比赛中淘汰了WG·格雷斯。

sentences.en: He got WG Grace out in a first class match.
sentences.zh: 所以那很厉害。

sentences.en: So that's good.
sentences.zh: 我想问题是，柯南·道尔并没有作为伟大恶作剧者的名声。

sentences.en: And I guess the question is, Conan Doyle doesn't have a reputation as a great hoaxer.
sentences.zh: 他实际上因为仙女照片事件而以骗局受害者的身份闻名。

sentences.en: He has a reputation actually as a victim of hoaxes because of obviously the fairies photographed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，基本上他什么都信。

sentences.en: Well, basically he believes everything.
sentences.zh: 而且他相信唯灵论。

sentences.en: And he believes in spiritualism.
sentences.zh: 他总是去参加降神会之类的无稽之谈。

sentences.en: He's always going to seances and nonsense like that.
sentences.zh: 他确实去。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，他去实施这个骗局看起来很奇怪……

sentences.en: So, I mean, him carrying out the hoax seems like an odd...
sentences.zh: 理论是，他想报复科学界对唯灵论的嘲笑。

sentences.en: The theory is that he wants revenge on the scientific establishment for mocking spiritualism.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这并非完全不可信。

sentences.en: I find that not entirely implausible.
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: Do you?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: It's completely implausible.
sentences.zh: 这完全站不住脚。

sentences.en: It's a mad theory.
sentences.zh: 这理论太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, I'll quote Stephen Jay Gould, the great evolutionary biologiSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我引用一下伟大的进化生物学家斯蒂芬·杰伊·古尔德的话。

sentences.en: What can one say of an evidence-free argument based on speculations about motive?
sentences.zh: 对于一个基于动机猜测、毫无证据的论点，人们能说什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, you can say it sounds very plausible like I've just done.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可以说它听起来非常合理，就像我刚才做的那样。

sentences.en: I mean, just because Stephen Jay Gould thinks it's implausible, you haven't convinced me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，仅仅因为斯蒂芬·杰伊·古尔德认为它不可信，你还没能说服我。

sentences.en: No, it's absolutely not the kind of thing that Conan Doyle would have done.
sentences.zh: 不，这绝对不是柯南·道尔会做的那种事。

sentences.en: Because as you said, he has no background as a hoaxer and he is absolutely the kind of person who would be hoaxed.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，他没有造假的背景，而且他绝对是那种会被人欺骗的人。

sentences.en: So, let's say that there are more plausible candidates to hand.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们说还有更合理的嫌疑人选。

sentences.en: Let's hear them.
sentences.zh: 说来听听。

sentences.en: So, let's look at some of them.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们来看看其中一些人。

sentences.en: So, what about one of the scientists studying Piltdown Man?
sentences.zh: 那么，研究皮尔当人的科学家之一怎么样？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So, there have been various suggestions.
sentences.zh: 所以，有各种各样的建议。

sentences.en: So, there's a guy called Arthur Keith who was a very celebrated anatomist, anthropologiSt.
sentences.zh: 有一个叫亚瑟·基思的人，他是一位非常著名的解剖学家和人类学家。

sentences.en: He was head of the Ahunterian and he'd started out very sceptical about Piltdown Man.
sentences.zh: 他是亨特博物馆的负责人，起初他对皮尔当人非常怀疑。

sentences.en: He then swung massively behind it, huge enthusiast for the idea that it was authentic.
sentences.zh: 后来他极力支持这一观点，非常热衷于它是真实存在的想法。

sentences.en: And then, when presented with the evidence in 1953, accepted that it was a fake.
sentences.zh: 然后，当1953年证据摆在面前时，他承认这是一个骗局。

sentences.en: He's all over the place.
sentences.zh: 他立场摇摆不定。

sentences.en: I mean, he doesn't know what he thinks.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他自己都不知道自己在想什么。

sentences.en: He is all over the place.
sentences.zh: 他完全是立场不稳。

sentences.en: And so, it has been suggested that this is a deliberate attempt to kind of obfuscate.
sentences.zh: 因此，有人认为这是一种蓄意的混淆视听。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Again, I think it's implausible.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我认为这不可信。

sentences.en: Then, there's an extraordinary character called Pierre Teilhard de Chardin who was a French Jesuit Darwinist paleontologiSt.
sentences.zh: 然后，还有一个非凡的人物，叫皮埃尔·泰亚尔·德·夏尔丹，他是一位法国耶稣会达尔文主义古生物学家。
zh_words: 皮埃尔·泰亚尔·德·夏尔丹

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: It's definitely him.
sentences.zh: 绝对是他。

sentences.en: There's no question in my mind.
sentences.zh: 我心里毫无疑问。

sentences.en: So, as a young man, he'd been posted to Sussex by the Jesuit superior.
sentences.zh: 所以，他年轻时被耶稣会上级派往苏塞克斯。

sentences.en: And because he was so interested in paleontology, he'd been fascinated by Piltdown to come and join the dig in 1912.
sentences.zh: 因为他对古生物学非常感兴趣，他被皮尔当遗址所吸引，于1912年加入挖掘工作。

sentences.en: You know, he joined Woodward and Dawson at the excavation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他加入了伍德沃德和道森的挖掘队。

sentences.en: Such French behaviour like dropping little bits of other bones in the thing while he's pretending to dig.
sentences.zh: 这种法国式的行为，就像在假装挖掘时往坑里扔点其他骨头碎片一样。

sentences.en: I can see it now.
sentences.zh: 我现在都能想象出来。

sentences.en: And he would go on.
sentences.zh: 而且他还会继续这样做。

sentences.en: He was involved in a dig that found a Java man equivalent in China.
sentences.zh: 他参与了一次挖掘，在中国发现了相当于爪哇人的化石。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Peking man, as it was called.
sentences.zh: 也就是所谓的北京人。

sentences.en: So, I can't quite remember what the reasons are for thinking that he might have done it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不太记得认为他可能做了这件事的理由是什么了。

sentences.en: But there are people who think that he did it.
sentences.zh: 但确实有人认为是他干的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And then some people have even suggested Arthur Smith Woodward, even though, obviously, he comes out of the whole affair looking an absolute idiot.
sentences.zh: 还有人甚至提到了亚瑟·史密斯·伍德沃德，尽管很明显，他在整件事中看起来像个彻头彻尾的傻瓜。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I don't believe a gaunt tall man would have done it, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我不相信一个瘦削高大的男人会做这种事。

sentences.en: With a beard like a goat.
sentences.zh: 还留着山羊胡子。

sentences.en: So, there's no evidence that any of these people were involved in it.
sentences.zh: 所以，没有证据表明这些人中的任何一个参与其中。

sentences.en: And in fact, there is only one scientist who does seem to have questions to answer.
sentences.zh: 事实上，只有一位科学家似乎有疑问需要解答。

sentences.en: This is a man called Martin Hinton, who in 1912 was working as a volunteer at the Natural History Museum underneath Woodward and really detested him, really disliked him.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫马丁·欣顿，1912年他在自然历史博物馆伍德沃德手下做志愿者，他非常厌恶他，真的很讨厌他。

sentences.en: And he goes on to have a very distinguished career.
sentences.zh: 后来他拥有了非常杰出的职业生涯。

sentences.en: He ends up as the museum's keeper of zoology.
sentences.zh: 他最终成为了博物馆的动物学馆长。

sentences.en: And in 1970, a trunk that had belonged to Hinton was found that Hinton had left in storage at the Natural History Museum.
sentences.zh: 1970年，人们发现了一个属于欣顿的行李箱，那是欣顿留在自然历史博物馆仓库里的。

sentences.en: And it was opened and it was found to contain animal teeth and bones that had been stained in a manner very reminiscent of the Piltdown bones.
sentences.zh: 打开后发现里面装有动物牙齿和骨头，其染色方式非常让人联想到皮尔当骨骼。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: What's the explanation?
sentences.zh: 有什么解释吗？

sentences.en: The theory has been advanced that he disliked Woodward so much that he wanted to make him look an idiot.
sentences.zh: 有人提出了一个理论，说他太讨厌伍德沃德了，所以想让他出丑。

sentences.en: He would have needed to enlist the other guy, though, wouldn't he?
sentences.zh: 但他需要拉拢另一个人，不是吗？

sentences.en: He would.
sentences.zh: 确实需要。

sentences.en: So, that's the flaw in the argument.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是这个论点的漏洞。

sentences.en: And so, essentially, there is really only one obvious suspect, which is the guy who initially found the bone, which is, of course, the boiled egg-headed country solicitor,
sentences.zh: 所以，本质上，真的只有一个明显的嫌疑人，就是最初发现骨头的那个人，当然，就是那个煮鸡蛋头型的乡村律师，

sentences.en: Charles Dawson.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·道森。

sentences.en: Jovial.
sentences.zh: 快活的。

sentences.en: Jovial, with a mischievous twinkle in his eye.
sentences.zh: 快活，眼里闪烁着顽皮的光芒。

sentences.en: Never trust a man with a twinkle in his eye.
sentences.zh: 永远不要相信一个眼里闪烁着光芒的人。

sentences.en: And he's always been the most plausible suspect.
sentences.zh: 他一直是最可疑的嫌疑人。

sentences.en: And there is now absolutely no doubt that it was him.
sentences.zh: 现在毫无疑问就是他。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: There really isn't a mystery.
sentences.zh: 真的没有什么悬念。

sentences.en: So, there are two brilliant books on Dawson that came out last 20 years by Mars Russell, brilliant archaeologist, specialist in the Iron Age now.
sentences.zh: 所以，过去20年里有两本关于道森的精彩著作，作者是马尔斯·拉塞尔，一位杰出的考古学家，现在是铁器时代的专家。

sentences.en: And these books combined conclusively prove it.
sentences.zh: 这两本书结合起来确凿地证明了这一点。

sentences.en: So, I'll quote him in his most recent book, The Piltdown Man Hoax Case Closed, which absolutely does what it says on the tin.
sentences.zh: 所以，我引用他最近的一本书《皮尔当人骗局：结案》，这本书名副其实。

sentences.en: So, Russell writes, the question of whether Dawson was in any way involved in the Piltdown controversy can no longer be in doubt.
sentences.zh: 拉塞尔写道，道森是否以任何方式参与了皮尔当争议的问题已不再有疑问。

sentences.en: He is the only person implicated at every stage of the fraud, and the only one with the means, opportunity, and, as far as we can ascertain,
sentences.zh: 他是唯一在欺诈的每个阶段都牵涉其中的人，也是唯一拥有手段、机会的人，据我们所知，

sentences.en: in the absence of surviving personal correspondence, or indeed of a signed confession, motive.
sentences.zh: 在没有幸存的个人信件，或者确实没有签署供词的情况下，他有动机。

sentences.en: And yet, Tom, he's a tremendous fellow.
sentences.zh: 然而，汤姆，他是个了不起的家伙。

sentences.en: Everybody says he's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 每个人都说他很聪明。

sentences.en: He's found all these amazing and very plausible artefacts in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 他过去发现了所有这些令人惊叹且非常合理的文物。

sentences.en: How could anyone possibly believe this?
sentences.zh: 怎么会有人相信这个？

sentences.en: It would sound a character for him, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 这听起来很符合他的性格，不是吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, despite the fact that, you know, the scientists who work on The Dig like him, it's clear that he has a very, very unscrupulous side.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管你知道，那些在挖掘现场工作的科学家喜欢他，但很明显他有非常非常不择手段的一面。

sentences.en: And he has made himself very unpopular with Sussex Antiquarian Circles.
sentences.zh: 而且他在苏塞克斯古物研究圈里非常不受欢迎。

sentences.en: So, I mentioned the Sussex Archaeological Society.
sentences.zh: 所以我提到了苏塞克斯考古学会。

sentences.en: He had had a massive bust up with them.
sentences.zh: 他和他们闹翻了。

sentences.en: And Castle Lodge, this wonderful house at the foot of Sussex Castle that he lives in, had originally been the headquarters of the Sussex Archaeological Society.
sentences.zh: 城堡小屋，那座他居住的位于苏塞克斯城堡脚下的美妙房子，最初是苏塞克斯考古学会的总部。

sentences.en: And they had employed him to negotiate them a better deal with the landlord.
sentences.zh: 他们雇佣他去和房东谈判，争取更好的条件。

sentences.en: And he'd gone behind their backs and negotiated a long-term contract for himself and then evicted the Sussex Archaeological Society.
sentences.zh: 结果他背着他们为自己谈下了一份长期合同，然后把苏塞克斯考古学会赶了出去。

sentences.en: Tom, I have to say, I think he's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我不得不说，我觉得他很聪明。

sentences.en: I love the sound of him.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢听关于他的事。

sentences.en: He and I would get on tremendously.
sentences.zh: 我和他会相处得非常融洽。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Well, so I said that he didn't seem to be doing much law, but that, I mean, that shows tremendous ability to leverage conveyancing skills.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以我说他似乎没怎么做法律工作，但这意味着他有极强的利用产权转让技能的能力。

sentences.en: He should have been leading the National Guard and the French Revolution, so that absolutely wet weekend Lafayette.
sentences.zh: 他本应该领导国民警卫队和法国大革命，而不是那个软弱无能的拉法耶特。

sentences.en: He'd have sorted it out.
sentences.zh: 他肯定能搞定。

sentences.en: So, there's that.
sentences.zh: 所以，就是这样。

sentences.en: But there's also, as you said, all these fines that have given him the moniker of the Wizard of Sussex.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，还有所有这些让他获得“苏塞克斯巫师”绰号的发现。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And basically, you know, magic, when you look at it, it always turns out not to be quite what it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你知道，当你审视魔法时，它总是显得不那么名副其实。

sentences.en: And it's the same with his fines.
sentences.zh: 他的发现也是一样。

sentences.en: So, Mars Russell has looked at all the fines he made and pretty conclusively demonstrated that at least 33 of them are clearly fakes.
sentences.zh: 所以，马尔斯·拉塞尔研究了他所有的发现，并相当确凿地证明其中至少有33个显然是赝品。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: So, in addition to Piltdown Man, I mentioned the fossil of the Cretaceous mammal.
sentences.zh: 所以，除了皮尔当人，我还提到了白垩纪哺乳动物的化石。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So, the whole basis for thinking that this mammal is a new, previously undiscovered species is the fact that its teeth are quite worn.
sentences.zh: 所以，认为这种哺乳动物是一个新的、以前未被发现的物种的全部依据，就是它的牙齿磨损得很厉害。

sentences.en: And when Russell went and looked at them, it turned out that they had been filed down in exactly the same way that the teeth of Piltdown Man had been filed down.
sentences.zh: 当拉塞尔去查看它们时，发现它们被锉磨的方式与皮尔当人的牙齿被锉磨的方式完全一样。

sentences.en: So, a deliberate fake.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个蓄意的伪造。

sentences.en: And what's interesting about that was that this creature was cast as a missing link.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这个生物被塑造成了一个缺失的环节。

sentences.en: So, very early on in Dawson's career, he's obviously already kind of moving along these lines.
sentences.zh: 所以，在道森职业生涯的早期，他显然已经沿着这些思路在行动了。

sentences.en: The Roman statuette, you remember that, that was made of cast iron?
sentences.zh: 那个罗马小雕像，你还记得吗，那是铸铁做的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: The reason it's made of cast iron is because it's a modern copy.
sentences.zh: 它之所以是铸铁做的，是因为它是现代仿制品。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: No one spotted this at the time?
sentences.zh: 当时没人发现吗？

sentences.en: No one spotted it at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时没人发现。

sentences.en: Because, well, we'll come to how he's able to get away with all this in a minute.
sentences.zh: 因为，好吧，我们一会儿再谈他是如何逃脱这一切的。

sentences.en: But just to continue the list, the brick, the axe, the boat, all doctored.
sentences.zh: 但继续列举清单，砖块、斧头、船，全都是伪造的。

sentences.en: The mummified toad inside a flint.
sentences.zh: 燧石里的木乃伊蟾蜍。

sentences.en: I mean, you said, I don't know how that's possible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你说过，我不知道这怎么可能。

sentences.en: It isn't possible.
sentences.zh: 这不可能。

sentences.en: It's clearly a fake.
sentences.zh: 这显然是伪造的。

sentences.en: So, basically, what he's doing over the course of his career, he's developed certain techniques.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，他在职业生涯中所做的是，他开发了某些技术。

sentences.en: And these are that, as with Piltdown Man, he always adopts a kind of studded vagueness as to where and when he'd made his finds.
sentences.zh: 这些技术就是，正如皮尔当人一样，他总是对自己的发现地点和时间采取一种含糊其辞的态度。

sentences.en: He's also constantly claiming that the finds had originally been made by anonymous workmen.
sentences.zh: 他还不断声称这些发现最初是由匿名工人做出的。

sentences.en: Who then, of course, can't be found because he's saying, you know, four years afterwards, you couldn't possibly find the workmen.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些工人后来就找不到了，因为他说，你知道，四年后，你根本不可能找到那些工人。

sentences.en: So, that kind of obscures the process.
sentences.zh: 所以，这掩盖了整个过程。

sentences.en: He's also unbelievably skillful at roping in academics who can serve him as his dupes.
sentences.zh: 他还极其擅长拉拢那些可以作为他棋子的学者。

sentences.en: So, Woodward would be the paradigm of this, but there are others as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，伍德沃德就是这方面的典型，但还有其他人。

sentences.en: And above all, what he's doing, which is what every confidence trickster does, is he is giving the victims what they want to find.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，他所做的，也就是每个骗子都会做的，就是给受害者他们想要发现的东西。

sentences.en: Because, of course, they will share in the discoveries, right?
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，他们会分享发现的成果，对吧？

sentences.en: But also, he knows the way their work is leading and he knows what they're anxious to find and he produces it.
sentences.zh: 而且，他知道他们的工作方向，知道他们急于发现什么，然后他就制造出来。

sentences.en: I mean, he is very knowledgeable of that paleontology.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他非常了解古生物学。

sentences.en: And so, he knows that what British scientists want more than anything else is a large-headed missing link found in Britain for all the reasons that we looked in the first half.
sentences.zh: 所以，他知道英国科学家最想要的是在英国发现一个大头缺失环节，原因就是我们在前半部分所看到的那些。

sentences.en: This is exactly what he serves up.
sentences.zh: 这正是他所提供的。

sentences.en: Now, you may ask, you know, what is his motive?
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会问，你知道，他的动机是什么？

sentences.en: And the motive, I think, is very clear.
sentences.zh: 我认为动机非常明确。

sentences.en: He wants, like all amateurs, professional status.
sentences.zh: 像所有业余爱好者一样，他想要职业地位。

sentences.en: He wants, specifically, I think, election to the Royal Society, which is the supreme body of British science.
sentences.zh: 我特别认为，他想要入选英国科学界的最高机构——皇家学会。

sentences.en: And he wants a knighthood.
sentences.zh: 他还想要一个爵位。

sentences.en: Like you.
sentences.zh: 像你一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, very similar.
sentences.zh: 嗯，非常相似。

sentences.en: I have a certain amount of a feeling for him.
sentences.zh: 我对他有一种某种程度上的共鸣。

sentences.en: And so, I think he's come to realise that to have a chance of winning either or both, he needs something really, really spectacular.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想他意识到要赢得其中之一或两者，他需要一些真正非常壮观的东西。

sentences.en: And this is where Piltdown Man comes in because, you know, the origins of humanity is such a massive theme that it would resonate sufficiently that it might get him the rewards.
sentences.zh: 这就是皮尔当人出现的原因，因为，你知道，人类起源是一个如此宏大的主题，它会产生足够的共鸣，从而可能为他赢得奖励。

sentences.en: And Miles Russell makes, I think, a completely convincing argument that actually he gets the idea for Piltdown Man when he was at that lunch with Conan Doyle in 1911,
sentences.zh: 马尔斯·拉塞尔提出了一个我认为完全令人信服的论点，即实际上他在1911年与柯南·道尔共进午餐时就有了皮尔当人的想法，

sentences.en: when Conan Doyle had told him about his plans for the lost world.
sentences.zh: 当时柯南·道尔告诉了他关于《失落的世界》的计划。

sentences.en: And they talked about missing links and ape men.
sentences.zh: 他们谈到了缺失的环节和猿人。

sentences.en: So, I'll read Russell.
sentences.zh: 所以，我读一下拉塞尔的话。

sentences.en: He says, this was Dawson's moment of revelation, the realisation that he had his big find.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是道森的启示时刻，他意识到自己有了大发现。

sentences.en: Much of his antiquarian career to date had been spent providing people in the academic community with transitional artefacts,
sentences.zh: 他迄今为止的大部分古物研究生涯都花在为学术界的人提供过渡性文物上，

sentences.en: missing links in the chain of technological development.
sentences.zh: 技术发展链条中缺失的环节。

sentences.en: But now, with Piltdown Man, he's going for the big one.
sentences.zh: 但现在，有了皮尔当人，他要干一票大的。

sentences.en: The ultimate missing link.
sentences.zh: 终极的缺失环节。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, he has the knowledge to know how this will resonate with the paleontological community.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他很清楚这会在古生物学界引起怎样的反响。

sentences.en: But he also, you know, he knows where to find a likely spot for the fraud to be staged.
sentences.zh: 但他也知道，去哪里找一个适合实施骗局的地点。

sentences.en: So, the quarry pit at Piltdown is very expertly chosen.
sentences.zh: 所以，皮尔当的采石坑选得非常专业。

sentences.en: Again, to quote Russell, what he needed was an apparently secure sequence of deposits of the right age for early humans.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，引用拉塞尔的话，他需要的是一个看起来可靠的、年代适合早期人类的沉积序列。

sentences.en: The reason for their disturbance, ideally road digging or quarrying, that would explain how the finds were noticed in the first place.
sentences.zh: 至于这些地层为何会被扰动，最好是修路或采石，这样就能解释为什么最初会发现这些东西。

sentences.en: And a landowner who was more than happy to allow additional excavation and investigation that happens on the property of someone that Dawson is a friend of.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果土地所有者非常乐意让人在自家地盘上进行额外的挖掘和调查，那就更好了，而这恰好发生在道森的一位朋友的地产上。

sentences.en: So, this is why he chooses the place that he does.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是他选择那个地方的原因。

sentences.en: And the final piece in this jigsaw puzzle, Dominic, I mean, it's literally a jigsaw puzzle, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，这块拼图的最后一块，我的意思是，这简直就是一块拼图，不是吗？

sentences.en: The shattered fragments of this skull with the mysterious thickness.
sentences.zh: 那些有着神秘厚度的破碎头骨残片。

sentences.en: He has access to a large array of sources, both legitimate and not, because of his role, you know, as both a dealer, but also he's involved in all these kind of various museuMs.
sentences.zh: 他因为自己的身份，既是古董商，又参与了各种博物馆的工作，所以他能接触到大量来源，无论合法的还是非法的。

sentences.en: And we know, for instance, that a medieval skull with Paget's disease had disappeared in the 1900s
sentences.zh: 我们知道，例如，一个患有佩吉特氏病的中古头骨在1900年代从黑斯廷斯博物馆消失了，

sentences.en: from the museum in Hastings, and Dawson had been on the committee of the Hastings Museum.
sentences.zh: 而道森当时就在黑斯廷斯博物馆的委员会里。

sentences.en: I think Dawson, to my mind, you see, unlike many of the listeners will think this is dreadful, but I think he's come out of this absolutely brilliantly.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，道森，你看，虽然很多听众会觉得这很可怕，但我认为他在这件事上表现得非常出色。

sentences.en: I think he sounds like such a splendid person.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他听起来是个了不起的人。

sentences.en: But my question is, I mean, he absolutely should have been given a knighthood for services to hoaxes.
sentences.zh: 但我的问题是，我的意思是，他绝对应该因为在骗局方面的贡献而被授予爵位。

sentences.en: To hoaxing.
sentences.zh: 为了行骗。

sentences.en: Yeah, but did he get the Royal Society membership in the knighthood?
sentences.zh: 是啊，但他拿到皇家学会会员资格和爵位了吗？

sentences.en: No, he didn't.
sentences.zh: 没有，他没拿到。

sentences.en: No, he died before he got either of them.
sentences.zh: 没有，他在得到这两者之前就去世了。

sentences.en: But he did die in the knowledge that this thing had been named after him.
sentences.zh: 但他去世时，确实知道这个东西是以他的名字命名的。

sentences.en: Yeah, he did.
sentences.zh: 是的，他知道。

sentences.en: And it must have been so satisfying.
sentences.zh: 那一定让他感到非常满足。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And there's that painting where he is the one who is closest to Darwin.
sentences.zh: 还有那幅画，画里他离达尔文最近。

sentences.en: Just imagine the glow he must have felt when he went to bed every night, knowing that he'd fooled the world.
sentences.zh: 试想一下，当他每晚睡觉时，想到自己愚弄了全世界，那种光荣感一定让他倍感满足。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: Well, possibly, or possibly he's in a state of constant trepidation that he's going to be rumbled.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许吧，或者他一直处于担心被揭穿的惶恐之中。

sentences.en: And that may well have been something that was kind of playing on him, because there is one remaining mystery, and this has to do with the cricket bat.
sentences.zh: 这很可能一直困扰着他，因为还有一个未解之谜，这与那根板球棒有关。

sentences.en: And Martin Hinton's trunk.
sentences.zh: 还有马丁·辛顿的行李箱。

sentences.en: And Chris Stringer, who we had on the show, talking about Neanderthals, he's at the Natural History Museum, one of the great specialists in prehistoric humans,
sentences.zh: 克里斯·斯特林格，我们节目请过他谈论尼安德特人，他在自然历史博物馆工作，是史前人类领域的顶尖专家之一，

sentences.en: he has a theory that provides a single solution to both those puzzles.
sentences.zh: 他有一个理论，为这两个谜题提供了一个统一的解决方案。

sentences.en: So his theory is that Martin Hinton had rumbled Piltdown Man as a fraud, and was aiming to tip off the culprit, and that this explains the cricket bat.
sentences.zh: 他的理论是，马丁·辛顿已经识破了皮尔当人是个骗局，并试图给罪魁祸首提个醒，这就是板球棒的由来。

sentences.en: He had basically deliberately planted the most absurd object that he could come up with.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是故意放了一个他能想到的最荒谬的物体。

sentences.en: And thinking that everyone would look at this cricket bat and say, this is obviously mad.
sentences.zh: 他以为每个人看到这根板球棒都会说，这显然是疯了。

sentences.en: But, to quote Stringer, Hinton had miscalculated, to his horror, instead of terminating the whole Piltdown saga,
sentences.zh: 但引用斯特林格的话，辛顿失算了，令他惊恐的是，这不仅没有终结整个皮尔当骗局，

sentences.en: this bizarre piece was heralded as the world's oldest bone implement.
sentences.zh: 这件离奇的东西反而被誉为世界上最古老的骨制工具。

sentences.en: And I think that this reflects very well on the British public, that they liked the idea of their prehistoric forebears playing cricket.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很好地反映了英国公众的心理，他们喜欢自己的史前祖先打板球的想法。

sentences.en: So, I think that, to an extent, you were right, that it's such an entertaining story, such an improbable story, that we should probably salute the man who made it all possible.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种程度上，你是对的，这是一个如此有趣、如此不可思议的故事，我们或许应该向让这一切成为可能的人致敬。

sentences.en: And to quote Miles Russell again,
sentences.zh: 再次引用迈尔斯·拉塞尔的话，

sentences.en: Charles Dawson, the most successful archaeological and antiquarian forger that the world has ever known.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·道森，这是世界上有史以来最成功的考古和古物造假者。

sentences.en: Well, hats off to Charles Dawson.
sentences.zh: 好吧，向查尔斯·道森致敬。

sentences.en: And Dominic, he was British, so hooray.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，他是英国人，所以万岁。

sentences.en: I'm actually prouder of him and of Britain.
sentences.zh: 比起故事开始时，我现在实际上更以他、更以英国为荣。

sentences.en: At the end of the story, then I was at the beginning, which is nice.
sentences.zh: 这感觉真不错。

sentences.en: So, very much a friend of the show, Charles Dawson.
sentences.zh: 所以，查尔斯·道森，真是我们节目的好朋友。

sentences.en: And thank you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，汤姆。

sentences.en: That was enormously good fun.
sentences.zh: 这真是太有趣了。

sentences.en: I enjoyed that a lot.
sentences.zh: 我很享受。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And obviously, on this podcast, we have an absolutely scrupulous attitude towards facts of history, as listeners to our episode on the Costa Rican Civil War will testify.
sentences.zh: 显然，在这个播客中，我们对历史事实有着极其严谨的态度，我们关于哥斯达黎加内战的那期节目听众可以作证。

sentences.en: We would never come up with nonsense in the hope of a knighthood.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会为了骗取爵位而编造胡言乱语。

sentences.en: No, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不会。

sentences.en: So, on that bombshell, thank you very much, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那么，带着这个重磅消息，非常感谢你，汤姆。

sentences.en: Superb stuff.
sentences.zh: 精彩的内容。

sentences.en: I think we should return to the subject of hoaxes in a future podcast, because there are many, many tremendous hoaxes, which would be fun to investigate.
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该在未来的播客中回到骗局这个话题，因为还有许多非常了不起的骗局，调查起来会很有趣。

sentences.en: But that's enough for now.
sentences.zh: 但现在就到这里吧。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, and goodbye.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
